subject: Changes in Parameters and R2 once Mediation is introduced?

messages.author: 3953ce039a72a3d4
messages.subject: Changes in Parameters and R2 once Mediation is introduced?
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to understand to which extent psychological factors mediate the association between parental and offspring education and stumbled into some strange results I can't really make sense of.

Consider a simplified model

s5_co_highest_edu ~ s2_co_factor_ability + s3_co_factor_scholastic_motivation   + s3_pa_edu 

Fitting this in lavaan leads to a rather satisfying R2 of 0.44 which is identical to what I obtain when I estimate it using OLS. The parameters are matched as well between both approaches. 

But then I introduce a mediation of the form

s2_co_factor_ability ~  s3_pa_edu 
s3_co_factor_scholastic_motivation  ~ s3_pa_edu 
s5_co_highest_edu ~ s2_co_factor_ability + s3_co_factor_scholastic_motivation   + s3_pa_edu 

While the parameters are still the same, the R2 is reduced by 0.03, down to 0.41. 

The whole thing gets even stranger if I want to model  s5_co_highest_edu not as continuous but instead as ordinal. In this case not just the R2 changes between the unmediated and the mediated model but also the parameters. Furthermore, the magnitude of change in the explained variance raises suspicions: The mediated model now increases the R2 by more than 0.08, from 0.47 to roughly 0.55. 

Can anyone help me to make sense of this behavior? 

Thanks!
Tobias

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Changes in Parameters and R2 once Mediation is introduced?
parts:
In your summary(), verify that you are estimating the residual covariance between mediators: 

s2_co_factor_ability ~~ s3_co_factor_scholastic_motivation 

That would allow for more explained variance in s5_co_highest_edu.  I don't think residual covariances between mediators are estimated by default (only among variables that are solely predictors and among variables that are solely outcomes), but there is no reason to assume s2_co_factor_ability & s3_co_factor_scholastic_motivation covary only because of s3_pa_edu.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
